page: Microsoft Azure E32s_v6 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Esv6 family, virtualized via Microsoft Hyper-V. It features 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 16 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz and includes a 260 MB L3 cache. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of RAM, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results indicate strong performance in specific workloads. The instance achieves top-tier status in text generation for small 135M LLM models at 390.88 tokens per second, alongside strong single-threaded gzip compression at 30.93 GB per second and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 180.09 GB per second. Geekbench single-core, image processing, and text processing scores also fall into the top 25 percent tier. Conversely, while CPU-bound tasks like the PassMark physics test score strongly, the PassMark memory score is weak, placing in the bottom 25 percent. Memory bandwidth is measured at 2173.18 GB per second for cached small blocks and drops to 146.81 GB per second for uncached large blocks.

The E32s_v6 offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require local NVMe storage. The lack of local storage requires reliance on external Premium Storage, which represents a key architectural tradeoff. Given its hardware profile, the server is suited for memory-intensive applications, database operations, static web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
